bindings.label: A woman in her 40s presented with a 3-year history of a complex progressive disorder characterized by emotional lability, cognitive decline, generalized ataxia, and autonomic dysfunction

Autonomic testing revealed abnormal cardiac parasympathetic function without orthostatic hypotension, patchy decrease in sweat output on quantitative sudomotor axon reflex test, and markedly abnormal thermoregulatory sweat test with near complete global anhidrosis
Patient denied paresthesias, dysesthesias, or loss of sensation
Brain MRI shows bilateral pulvinar hyperintensity and diffuse volume loss
CSF analysis shows elevated protein without pleocytosis
Patient has prion disease (e.g., sporadic or variant Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease)
Prion disease (e.g., sporadic or variant Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease)
Hereditary spinocerebellar ataxia with autonomic and cognitive involvement
Genetic testing shows a positive pseudo-α-galactosidase allele, interpreted as incidental and not explaining the phenotype
Prion-related tests (RT-QuIC, EEG, and PRNP analysis) are pending or unavailable
The 3-year clinical course is atypical for prion disease
No toxic exposure or metabolic derangement has been identified
CSF 14-3-3 protein testing is unavailable or pending
